newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower, just above day's lows.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower, just above day's lows.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled lower and just above the day's lows on spillover from losses in CBOT soybeans, hedging tied to increased country movement and small speculative selling, traders said.
"I think some of this is due to hedging -- we've been seeing movement on and off over the last couple of days," a trader said. "Plus there's really no buying in this market."

Wheat faltered early after soybeans opened sharply lower on news Taiwan was canceling tenders to import soy and corn. A late rally lifted beans off their daily lows but did not lend much support to KCBT wheat, traders said.
Traders also said some of Friday's selling by commission houses was probably tied to smaller speculators.

"I think when you look at the players' sheet you see a lot of small sales by a lot of people. That to me suggests that we had a bunch of retail clients selling five- or 10-lots," another KCBT trader said.
KCBT wheat settled 3-3/4 to ten cents per bushel lower, with May down 10 cents at $4.13-1/4. May had been as low as $4.11-1/2. July lost 8-3/4 cents to settle at $3.83-1/2.

Commodity brokerage Benson-Quinn was a featured player, buying 1.5 million July bushels but also selling 2.5 million May and one million July. E. D. & F. Man International sold two million May and 800,000 July, and at least one trader guessed that the sale was related to country movement.
